<reason>Side A won by successfully distinguishing "limiting bans" from "banning bans," thereby neutralizing CON's sovereignty argument and exposing that CON's voluntary alternative fails to stop pre-emptive bans. A's rebuttals were sharper, particularly in answering the pressure questions about the 72-hour enforcement gap with the "automatic sunset" mechanism, while B admitted its system offers no remedy in that window.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The Rebuttal 2 exchange where Side A answered the pressure questions: A4.1 explained that automatic expiry operates before any tribunal ruling, halting the cascade through pre-commitment, while A4.4 exposed that CON offered no remedy for pre-emptive bans and no enforceable limit it would accept, revealing that CON defends unlimited closure rather than emergency measures.</best_rebuttal>
